subject.title: fix(update): dev channel update builds from an unverified checkout at the git install path

question: Should package-to-dev conversion permanently refuse every pre-existing `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`, including an empty directory and a canonical-looking OpenClaw checkout, reclaiming only a path authenticated by both updater-owned state and the in-checkout marker?
rationale: This intentionally changes an existing upgrade path to fail closed in order to protect a code-execution trust boundary; source review cannot determine the acceptable operator-impact tradeoff without updater-owner intent.

options.title: Approve fail-closed conversion policy
options.body: Keep refusal of all unowned existing destinations, document the move-or-choose-new-path recovery, and require final-head proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve an existing-directory path
options.body: Define a separately reviewed migration or explicit opt-in path for existing package-to-dev destinations, accepting the additional trust-boundary design and maintenance burden.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed conversion policy
recommendation.body: Keep refusal of all unowned existing destinations, document the move-or-choose-new-path recovery, and require final-head proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied PR discussion directly requests this updater compatibility and security-boundary decision from vincentkoc.
